findings.title: Current-page own-status capture (BrowserTab.lastMainDocumentResponseCapture) is never invalidated when a new document commits WITHOUT its own Document response, so the PREVIOUS page's own 404 is reported as the current page's broken request (coversWholeDocument:true)
findings.repro: runtime.navigate(own404 page) -> runtime.navigate(X) -> runtime.audit(sid, {}) where X commits with no Network.responseReceived(type=Document): about:blank, a failed navigation (connection refused -> chrome-error page), or Back to a bfcache-restored page

rates.bfcache Back: current 5/5; pre-fix emulation ALSO 5/5 (pre-existing, but through a different path: pre-fix scoped since=timeOrigin of the original load, so the 404 row from the network ring buffer leaked; escalation-1 closes that path but the stale capture re-adds it)

rates.mcp: MCP stdio, 10 trials each: own404->about:blank 9/10, own404->dead-host 10/10, home->browser.click(broken link)->browser.go_back->browser.audit 10/10; coversWholeDocument:true in all 30 (probe-a51-mcp.json)

findings.cause: setupCommitTracking's Network.responseReceived handler overwrites lastMainDocumentResponseCapture only when a new Document response arrives for the main frame id (stable across navigations); Page.frameNavigated never clears or checks it (e.g. by loaderId). runtime.audit() current-page mode takes tab.getLastMainDocumentResponse() as the first-priority own-status source and pushes it into brokenRequests if status>=400.
findings.fixDirection: Invalidate the tab-level capture on every main-frame Page.frameNavigated whose frame.loaderId differs from the loaderId of the captured Network.responseReceived (both events carry loaderId), instead of relying on a later Document response to overwrite it. A response-less commit (about:blank, chrome-error, bfcache restore) then yields no live capture and falls through to the URL-match fallback. Add unit tests for all three shapes and a live case per shape.

findings.severity: minor (false-clean regression; narrow shape: Back/Forward to a bfcache-restored page; MCP/SDK only)
findings.title: A bfcache restore fires a main-frame Page.frameNavigated (type BackForwardCacheRestore), which moves lastMainFrameCommitAt to the RESTORE instant, so a restored document's own load-time findings are scoped out while coversWholeDocument stays true
findings.repro: navigate(A: own console.error + own fetch 404) -> navigate(clean) -> goBack (pageshow.persisted===true) -> audit(sid,{})

findings.fixDirection: On Page.frameNavigated with type BackForwardCacheRestore, either report coversWholeDocument:false (the restored document's pre-freeze activity is outside the scope window), or scope by the document's original commit instant (keyed by loaderId) while excluding the interval it spent in bfcache.

verdictReason: Escalation-1's core claim holds: GAP-278 (T11 noisy->clean->audit()) is fixed, 0/90 leaked across runtime+MCP x 0/150/800ms plus 0/90 own-finding drops; GAP-279 closes live (60/60 vs 6/30 pre-fix); GAP-280 closes (M7/M9/M10 killed by RA16/RA18/RA17); GAP-274 bound holds in fresh processes (2.56-2.58s vs 31.6s unbounded). The tab-lifetime mechanism survives long-lived/close/multi-tab/adoption/interleave attacks. The FAIL is A5-1 (major): the new tab-level own-status capture is never invalidated on a response-less commit, so the previous page's own 404 is reported as the current page's broken request (coversWholeDocument:true). This is the spec's T11/B1 contamination class. It reproduces deterministically: about:blank and a dead-host navigation are REGRESSIONS (0/5 pre-fix), and click-broken-link -> go_back -> audit is 10/10 via MCP. A5-2 (minor) is a companion bfcache false-clean regression.
